subject: Re: Redwood pricing & procurement path — PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood pricing & procurement path — PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated

Hi Samantha — thanks again for today’s call. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Procurement readiness: you mentioned Acme prefers PO on file for enterprise buys; procurement team (Raj) would need our W-9, SOC 2 Type II report, and a standard PO/terms flow.
- Commercial path options we discussed:
  * Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest to go-live, usage-based pricing (on-demand), supports card or invoiced PO for committed monthly spend.
  * Dedicated (reserved capacity) — predictable throughput and guaranteed capacity; typically requires a monthly commit (reserved seats/GPU hours) and invoiced PO.
  * Private (VPC/on-prem) — longer procurement cycle, platform fee + deployment services; usually enterprise contract and SOW.
- Key procurement asks from your team: PO vs card preference (PO preferred), approval SLA (30 days), and marketplace listing interest (AWS Marketplace mentioned).

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a short procurement checklist and a high-level quote for both Hosted (on-demand + 20% commit discount) and Dedicated (12-month commit pricing).
2) Marissa will confirm required legal docs for PO flow and handle invoice terms.
3) If marketplace is important, we can connect you to our partner team — that adds ~2–3 weeks to procurement onboarding.

Attaching the Hosted vs Dedicated overview and a procurement checklist for your procurement team to review. I’ll follow up with a formal quote by Monday.

Appreciate the time — let me know if I missed anything.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood-Hosted-vs-Dedicated-Overview.pdf, Acme-Procurement-Checklist.xlsx

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing & procurement path — PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated

Thanks Aditya — this is great and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from procurement (looping in Raj):

- PO process: We do prefer PO/invoice for anything above $10k monthly; below that we can use company card.
- Approval timeline: Standard is ~30 calendar days once we get a clean quote and W-9; faster if there’s a marketplace SKU (our procurement team uses marketplace billing where possible).
- Security docs: please include SOC 2 and Data Processing Agreement (DPA) — we’ll need to attach them to the PO packet.
- Marketplace: yes, having an AWS Marketplace listing would simplify internal billing. Interested in understanding if Redwood can provide a marketplace billing option for hosted or dedicated.

We’ll review the attachments and expect your quote.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Platforms, Acme Retail

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing & procurement path — PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated

Hi Samantha / Raj — quick answers inline to help your procurement team: 

- PO threshold: noted — we’ll structure the quote so Hosted on-demand shows estimated spend; we’ll also include a 12-month committed option for Dedicated that meets your PO threshold.
- Marketplace: Redwood currently supports AWS Marketplace for our Hosted API; Dedicated via marketplace is supported for select customers but may require an ISV procurement step. If Marketplace is a blocker, we can flag that and prioritize a listing request.
- Security docs: attaching SOC 2 Type II and DPA stub. Marissa — can you confirm the W-9 and standard PO terms doc are ready to share?

Next steps on our side:
- I’ve attached a draft quote (Redwood-Quote-ACME-20260321.pdf) with two lines: Hosted (on-demand & committed discount) and Dedicated (12-month commit). It includes both card and PO billing options in the notes.
- If you’d like to proceed via PO, please send Raj’s procurement contact and we’ll open the invoice account and share payment instructions.

Would you be available for a 20-min follow-up on Monday to walk procurement through the quote?

Best,
Aditya

Attachments: Redwood-Quote-ACME-20260321.pdf, SOC2-Report.pdf, DPA.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing & procurement path — PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated

Aditya — putting together the paperwork and timeline below so we can enable PO invoicing quickly for Acme: 

- Action items for Redwood Ops:
  * Confirm W-9 and remittance address (I have the W-9 on file; will attach to the HubSpot deal).
  * Prepare standard invoice terms (Net 30) and include our SOC 2 and DPA docs in the procurement packet.
  * Marketplace: I’ll check with partnerships on whether ACME can use AWS Marketplace for Hosted; if required we’ll start the ISV listing request — expect 2–3 weeks.
- Pricing notes:
  * Hosted: recommend starting on Hosted (on-demand) for proofs and early dev — lower friction. Provide a 20% discount if they commit to a 3-month spend target.
  * Dedicated: recommend if Acme needs predictable latency and higher throughput — requires 12-month commit; we should offer a 15% commit discount and invoice billing only.

I’ll produce the formal PO packet and send to Aditya by EOD Monday so procurement has everything for a quick review.

-Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-21T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing & procurement path — PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated

Hi Samantha / Raj — following up with the PO packet and next steps. Attached are: Redwood-Quote-ACME-20260321.pdf (hosted + dedicated options), Acme-Procurement-Checklist.xlsx, and the Hosted vs Dedicated overview.

Summary for procurement:
- Preferred path: Start on Hosted (on-demand) for dev + pilot — estimated month 1 spend $6k (card ok) then move to committed Hosted or Dedicated once usage stabilizes.
- If you want Dedicated now to meet performance targets, our recommended commercial path is a 12-month commit with Net 30 invoicing and a 15% commit discount. Dedicated requires a signed PO and SOW.
- Marketplace: we can enable AWS Marketplace for Hosted quickly; Dedicated marketplace listing is possible but may add 2–3 weeks.

Next steps:
1) Raj — if Acme will proceed with PO for Dedicated, please send a purchase order PDF and the billing contact.
2) If you prefer Hosted on-card to start, confirm card details or let us know and we’ll provision access.
3) Marissa will open the invoice account and share the W-9 and invoice instructions once Raj confirms PO path.

I’ve also included a DocuSign link for the quote (https://docusign.com/abcd-1234-quote) if you want to sign the quote and SOW electronically.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk procurement through anything.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
